import pytest

# Import the public function and the internal helpers for direct comparison
from slugify.slugify import slugify


# Helper to check if a string contains only ASCII characters
def _is_ascii(s: str) -> bool:
    return all(ord(ch) < 128 for ch in s)


def test_slugify__invalid_algorithm_raises():
    """
    Passing an unsupported algorithm should raise ValueError with the correct message.
    """
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        slugify("test", algorithm="invalid")
    assert "algorithm must be 'legacy' or 'modern'" in str(excinfo.value)


def test_slugify__max_length_truncation_word_boundary():
    """
    Verify that max_length truncates correctly with and without word_boundary.
    """
    text = "one-two-three-four"
    # With word_boundary=True the cut must not split a word
    result_boundary = slugify(
        text,
        max_length=10,
        word_boundary=True,
        algorithm="legacy",
    )
    # "one-two" is length 7, adding "-three" would exceed 10, so expect "one-two"
    assert result_boundary == "one-two"

    # With word_boundary=False the cut is hard at max_length characters
    result_hard = slugify(
        text,
        max_length=10,
        word_boundary=False,
        algorithm="legacy",
    )
    # First 10 characters of the slugified string "one-two-th..."
    assert result_hard == "one-two-th"

    # Same checks for the modern algorithm to catch bugs where algorithm selection fails
    result_boundary_mod = slugify(
        text,
        max_length=10,
        word_boundary=True,
        algorithm="modern",
    )
    assert result_boundary_mod == "one-two"

    result_hard_mod = slugify(
        text,
        max_length=10,
        word_boundary=False,
        algorithm="modern",
    )
    assert result_hard_mod == "one-two-th"


def test_slugify__unicode_allowed_vs_transliterated():
    """
    When allow_unicode=True the output retains non‑ASCII characters after NFKC.
    When allow_unicode=False the output is transliterated to pure ASCII.
    """
    text = "Привет мир"  # "Hello world" in Russian

    # Legacy algorithm
    unicode_legacy = slugify(text, allow_unicode=True, algorithm="legacy")
    # Exact expected legacy Unicode slug (lowercase Cyrillic, hyphen separator)
    assert unicode_legacy == "привет-мир"

    ascii_legacy = slugify(text, allow_unicode=False, algorithm="legacy")
    # Exact expected legacy ASCII slug
    assert ascii_legacy == "privet-mir"

    # Modern algorithm – ensure the branch is exercised and behaves sensibly
    unicode_modern = slugify(text, allow_unicode=True, algorithm="modern")
    # Should still contain non‑ASCII characters after NFKC normalization
    assert not _is_ascii(unicode_modern)

    ascii_modern = slugify(text, allow_unicode=False, algorithm="modern")
    # Should be ASCII after transliteration
    assert _is_ascii(ascii_modern)
    # The transliterated form should match the expected ASCII slug
    assert ascii_modern == "privet-mir"


def test_slugify__legacy_default_behavior():
    """
    Default call uses the legacy algorithm.
    Expect lower‑casing, hyphen separator and HTML entities decoded.
    """
    text = "Hello & World"
    expected = "hello-world"
    result = slugify(text)  # default algorithm is 'legacy'
    assert result == expected

    # Ensure the modern algorithm path is reachable and does not raise
    # (this would fail if the check for 'modern' was broken).
    slugify(text, algorithm='modern')


def test_slugify__stopwords_and_save_order():
    """
    Stopwords should be removed. With save_order=True the remaining words keep
    their original order; with save_order=False the order may differ.
    """
    text = "the quick brown fox a jumps over the lazy dog"
    stopwords = ("the", "a")
    # Preserve order
    ordered = slugify(
        text,
        stopwords=stopwords,
        save_order=True,
        algorithm="legacy",
    )
    # Expected order after removal of stopwords
    assert ordered == "quick-brown-fox-jumps-over-lazy-dog"

    # Do not preserve order
    unordered = slugify(
        text,
        stopwords=stopwords,
        save_order=False,
        algorithm="legacy",
    )
    # Stopwords must still be absent
    for sw in stopwords:
        assert sw not in unordered.split("-")
    # The set of words should be the same as in the ordered case
    assert set(unordered.split("-")) == {"quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps", "over", "lazy", "dog"}
    # No assertion about order difference; legacy may preserve order.


def test_slugify__modern_algorithm_path():
    """
    Verify that the modern algorithm path respects stopwords and the
    max_length character budget.
    """
    # Input contains several words, some of which are stopwords.
    text = "Alpha beta gamma delta epsilon"
    # The modern algorithm should remove the stopwords 'beta' and 'delta',
    # lowercase the remaining words, and join them with the default separator.
    result = slugify(
        text,
        algorithm="modern",
        stopwords=["beta", "delta"],
        max_length=20,          # generous enough to keep the whole result
        lowercase=True,
    )
    # Expected slug after stopword removal and normalisation.
    expected = "alpha-gamma-epsilon"
    assert result == expected
    # The emitted‑character length budget must not be exceeded.
    assert len(result) <= 20
